cards.subject: The Homily at a Sunday Mass, seen from across the nave at the height of a tall carved wooden pulpit fixed to a stone pillar, with a carved sounding board above it. In the pulpit, the priest, in a white-and-gold chasuble over a white alb, stands in profile and preaches, one hand resting on the pulpit's rail and the other open toward the people, his face earnest and kind. Below him the congregation sits in the wooden pews, small, faces turned up to listen: a mother with a sleeping baby, an old farmer, schoolchildren in a row. Far off, the sanctuary with the altar, its crucifix and lit candles. Late-morning light slants across the pillars. Attentive, warm. Keep everything inside the pointed arch.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: The priest gives the Homily 'standing at the chair or at the ambo itself or, if appropriate, in another worthy place' (GIRM 136): here a pulpit, which keeps the card apart from the ambo of the readings. cards.subject: The Creed at a Sunday Mass, seen from the side of the sanctuary looking across the front of the nave. cards.subject: The Preparation of the Gifts at a Sunday Mass, seen close from the side of the altar, in profile. The priest, in a white-and-gold chasuble over a white alb, stands at the altar facing it and holds a golden paten with a large white host slightly raised above the altar with both hands, just above the white corporal; beside the corporal stand a golden chalice with a folded white purificator and the open Missal on a small stand, its pages showing no letters. At the corner of the altar a server in cassock and surplice waits with the glass cruets of wine and water on a small tray. Beyond, soft and far, the congregation sits in the pews; a young couple who carried up the gifts walk back down the aisle. Warm candlelight, quiet offering. Keep everything inside the pointed arch.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: The corporal, purificator, chalice and Missal are placed on the altar and the faithful bring up the bread and wine (GIRM 73, 139–140); the priest 'holds it slightly raised above the altar with both hands and says quietly' the blessing of the excerpt, then the minister presents the cruets (GIRM 141–142; the Order of Mass rubric). The people sit (GIRM 43). 'Slightly raised', not the elevation: the paten stays just above the altar.

cards.subject: The Sanctus at a Sunday Mass, seen from the choir stalls at the side of the sanctuary, close to the altar. The priest, in a white-and-gold chasuble over a white alb, stands at the altar facing it, in profile, his hands joined, singing. Behind and above the altar rises a tall gilded reredos painted on a gold ground with rows of angels and six-winged red seraphim, all turned in adoration toward its centre, where a carved crucifix stands. Two servers in cassock and surplice stand at the side with hands joined. Beyond the altar rail, the congregation stands and sings, small. Candlelight glints on the gold. Jubilant, heavenly, one song with the angels. Keep everything inside the pointed arch.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: At the end of the Preface the priest 'joins his hands and, together with all those present, sings or says aloud the Sanctus' (GIRM 148), the acclamation 'by which the whole congregation, joining with the heavenly powers', takes part in the Eucharistic Prayer (GIRM 79b); all still stand (GIRM 43). The seraphim of Isaiah 6 on the reredos stand for those heavenly powers, as painting, not vision.

cards.subject: The Epiclesis, seen close from just behind and to the right of the priest, looking over his shoulder down onto the altar. The priest, in a white-and-gold chasuble over a white alb, stands at the middle of the altar facing it, his two hands held out together, palms down, over the offerings: on the white corporal, a golden paten with a large white host and a golden chalice. The open Missal on its stand beside them, pages showing no letters; the crucifix and tall lit candles rise beyond. High above the altar, in a round stained-glass window, the Holy Spirit as a white dove in golden rays, and a soft light falls from it onto the gifts. On the altar step below, a server in cassock and surplice kneels holding a small bell. The faithful kneel in the nave, unseen but for a hush. Still, expectant, luminous. Keep everything inside the pointed arch.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: In the Second Eucharistic Prayer the priest 'joins his hands and, holding them extended over the offerings' says the epiclesis, then makes the Sign of the Cross over the bread and chalice together (the Order of Mass rubric; GIRM 79c: the Church implores the power of the Holy Spirit on the gifts). A little before the Consecration a minister may ring a small bell (GIRM 150); the faithful kneel after the Sanctus (GIRM 43, USCCB). The dove is glass in the church's window.

sources.title: GIRM ch. 2, nos. 43, 79 (kneeling after the Sanctus; the epiclesis)

cards.subject: The Consecration at Mass, seen straight on from the foot of the altar steps, the altar the centre. At a white-and-gold high altar with six tall lit candles and a crucifix, the priest, in a white-and-gold chasuble over a white alb, seen from behind, facing the altar, raises the white Host high above his head with both hands. On the step at the right a server in cassock and white surplice kneels and rings a small bell; at the left a kneeling thurifer swings a smoking thurible toward the Host. Soft golden rays fall from above onto the Host. At the very bottom of the arch, the heads and shoulders of the faithful kneeling in the front pew, seen from behind. Figures small in the scene. Adoring, still. Keep everything inside the pointed arch.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: After the words over the bread the priest 'shows the consecrated host to the people, places it again on the paten, and genuflects in adoration' (the Order of Mass rubric, Eucharistic Prayer II; GIRM 79d); a minister rings the small bell at each elevation according to local custom, and if incense is used a minister incenses the host when it is shown (GIRM 150). The faithful kneel (GIRM 43, USCCB). Composed as the x_consecration test draft (2026-09-29), without its server lifting the chasuble's hem, which the rubrics don't give.

cards.subject: The Mystery of Faith at a Sunday Mass, seen from a side aisle at the front of the nave. In the foreground, half-length and in profile, the faithful kneel in a wooden pew and sing the acclamation, faces lifted toward the altar: an old woman with a rosary wound through her joined hands, a young father, a girl in a white veil. Beyond them, up the sanctuary steps and seen at an angle, the priest, in a white-and-gold chasuble over a white alb, stands at the altar facing it with his hands joined; on the corporal before him the golden chalice and the paten with the white Host, the tall candles burning on either side. cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: After the Consecration, when the priest, having shown the chalice and genuflected, has said The mystery of faith, 'the people pronounce the acclamation, using one of the prescribed formulas' (GIRM 151; the Order of Mass rubric), still kneeling until after the Amen (GIRM 43, USCCB). The acclamation is the people's, so the card is on them, as on the Responsorial Psalm.
